open_points.subject: Owner / staff actor
open_points.text: “Owner / staff” and “staff hold a staff credential”, while “the owner” alone administers the host, configuration and secrets
open_points.question: Are owner and staff distinct principals, who qualifies as staff, and may staff use the API directly or only through owner-configured tools such as the frontend server and operator?
options: Owner and staff are the same principal
Staff are separately authorized people who may receive the shared credential
Staff act only through tools that hold the credential
open_points.default_guess: Treat the owner and authorized staff as distinct people with equal Registry action permissions, normally acting through credential-holding tools.

open_points.subject: Operator actor and model-provider boundary
open_points.text: “Operator — `onboard_object`, or an agent preparing a client message” and “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model”
open_points.question: Does the model-provider disclosure apply only to an AI agent, or also to every execution of the `onboard_object` script; and which component actually transmits the contact fields to the provider?
options: Only AI-agent operations transmit fields to a model provider
Both `onboard_object` and AI-agent operations transmit fields
Transmission depends on how the operator tool is run
open_points.default_guess: Treat `onboard_object` as a non-model API client and apply the provider disclosure only when an AI agent performs the operation.

open_points.subject: Operator access to secrets
open_points.text: The operator “holds no service token” and an agent “works with the owner's own access to Registry's host”, while configuration containing service tokens is “readable only by the owner and the Registry process”
open_points.question: Can an operator agent using the owner's host access read Registry configuration and therefore obtain service tokens, or is its host access technically restricted to the store and staff credential?
options: The agent has owner-equivalent host access and can read all configured secrets
The agent runs under restricted access that cannot read Registry configuration
‘Holds no service token’ means it is not an assigned holder even though it can read tokens
open_points.default_guess: Treat the agent as owner-equivalent on the host and therefore able to read the configured secrets, while not using service tokens as its API identity.
